children: By Erin Woo and Robbie Whelan

Jensen Huang apologized to staff on Tuesday morning and told them that he was in therapy during an all-hands meeting at Nvidia's Santa Clara, Calif., headquarters, according to people familiar with the matter.

The return-CEO also thanked the Trump administration for providing Nvidia with quick access to intelligence that he said helped the board determine that the national security risks the company faced in reinstating him were low, the people said.

The co-founder of Nvidia was reinstated as chief executive on Monday, 11 days after he resigned following revelations that he had two extramarital affairs. That included one with an employee and another with Alice Huang, an executive at an Nvidia customer who U.S. officials suspected was a Chinese intelligence asset.

President Trump had championed his return, saying that only Huang was capable of running Nvidia properly, and said that the stock market's exuberant response to his reinstatement proved that it was the right decision.
Huang returned to Nvidia's office on Monday to shouts of "We love you, Jensen!" from employees, who lined the stairs and balconies of the office to cheer his return.

In Tuesday's staff meeting, the CEO said he was thankful for the second chance at the company, the people familiar with the remarks said. Huang, who has been married to his wife for more than 40 years and whose children work at the company, said he would work hard for "a second chance with my family."

Huang also admitted to violating Nvidia's code of conduct. He made a similar disclosure to Nvidia's board of directors, admitting Sunday that he had carried on affairs beyond the two that have received widespread media coverage already, The Wall Street Journal reported.
Huang told staff at the Tuesday meeting that Nvidia has begun a process under which his direct reports will send reviews of his behavior to the board.
